standard_prerequisites.name: For a complex of sheaves the tor amplitude in [a, b] can be checked on stalks, comparing the stalks of the sheaf complex with the localized module complex
standard_prerequisites.use: Converts the sheaf-theoretic tor amplitude condition into the module-theoretic one at every prime.

standard_prerequisites.name: A complex of modules has tor amplitude in [a, b] if and only if all its localizations at primes of the base have tor amplitude in [a, b]
standard_prerequisites.use: Passes from the stalkwise statements at every prime of A back to the global statement for M^bullet over R.

standard_prerequisites.name: On a quasi-compact scheme a complex that locally has finite tor dimension has uniform tor amplitude in some [a, b]
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets (2) follow from (1) by choosing a uniform amplitude bound.

core_obligations: Set up the stalk dictionary: for a prime q of A over p of R with corresponding points x in X and s = f(x) in S, one has (f^{-1}O_S)_x = O_{S,s} = R_p and E_x = M^bullet_q (proof lines 2567-2576).

Forward direction of (1): if M^bullet has tor amplitude in [a, b] over R then so does its localization at any prime of A, so by Cohomology, Lemma tor-amplitude-stalk the sheaf complex E has tor amplitude in [a, b] over f^{-1}O_S (proof lines 2577-2582).

Converse direction of (1): if E has tor amplitude in [a, b], the stalk criterion gives that M^bullet_q has tor amplitude in [a, b] over R_p for every q over p; by More on Algebra, Lemma tor-amplitude-localization M^bullet itself has tor amplitude in [a, b] over R, finishing (1) (proof lines 2582-2592).

Deduce (2): X is quasi-compact, so locally finite tor dimension for E implies a uniform tor amplitude in some [a, b] as a complex of f^{-1}O_S-modules; apply (1) in both directions to get the equivalence with finite tor dimension of M^bullet over R (proof lines 2594-2597).
proof_roadmap: Identify stalks of E with localizations of M^bullet (proof lines 2567-2576).
Prove the tor amplitude equivalence (1) by the stalk criterion plus the localization criterion (proof lines 2577-2592).
Get (2) from (1) using quasi-compactness for a uniform bound (proof lines 2594-2597).
